excluded_skills.name: adding-a-skill
excluded_skills.reason: Repo-internal tooling for BuilderIO/skills itself, with a BROKEN DEPENDENCY CLOSURE at this pin and no applicability to a Go project. Its frontmatter scopes it explicitly: 'Use in the BuilderIO/skills repo whenever adding, updating, publishing, documenting, validating, or wiring a public skill.' Nine of its file references point at `../agent-native/framework/**` — a sibling private repo that is absent from the clone (packages/core/src/cli/skills.ts, packages/skills/src/built-in-apps.ts, src/index.ts, src/index.spec.ts, src/sync-with-core.spec.ts, packages/skills/dist/cli.js). Worse, its validation step hardcodes a foreign absolute path from a specific developer's laptop: SKILL.md:51 `python3 /Users/steve/.codex/skills/.system/skill-creator/scripts/quick_validate.py skills/<skill-name>`. It also duplicates the role of the already-installed skill-creator-anthropic and the Claude Code builtin skill-creator.

excluded_skills.name: efficient-fable
excluded_skills.reason: TRUE DUPLICATE of efficient-frontier, which I recommend installing. efficient-frontier's own frontmatter says 'Apply the same orchestration as `/efficient-fable` to any high-cost frontier model' — same five-step delegation pattern, same handoff-packet fields, same stop conditions, same four Common Scenarios (research/coding/testing/debugging), same vet-before-trusting review loop. The only differences are branding to one specific model ('Reserve Fable for...', trigger is 'when running Claude Fable') and an added Claims section asserting 'up to 3-5x more cost-efficient and 2-4x faster' plus 'Good launch copy' — marketing, not methodology. Installing both would put two near-identical descriptions in the trigger space and make skill selection ambiguous for no capability gain.

excluded_skills.name: quick-recap
excluded_skills.reason: No material capability for any lane in the selection rule — it is purely a response-formatting convention (end every response with a 🟢/🟡/🔴 status line under 100 characters). It contributes nothing to Go architecture, Twitch mechanisms, persistence, testing, security, documentation, GitHub workflows, dashboard design, browser QA, or durable knowledge. Independently, its 'Installer Behavior' section instructs the agent to mutate governed files — 'When installing this skill, prefer adding the managed `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md` block unless the user opts out' — which collides head-on with the standing rule that no agent message can authorize changing CLAUDE.md, and with the authority chain in which a skill (level 3) may never widen what it may touch. Excluding is cleaner than patching a skill whose remaining content is a four-rule emoji convention.

excluded_skills.name: rewind
excluded_skills.reason: Irrelevant platform and no capability-lane match. It is a retrieval front end for Clips Rewind local screen-recording memory and requires, per its own First-Run Setup, 'the signed Clips Desktop app on macOS plus a local agent connection' — this environment is Linux (Platform: linux, Linux 6.18.5), so the hard prerequisite can never be satisfied here. Every operation is a Screen Memory MCP tool (screen_memory_status, screen_memory_search_chapters, screen_memory_recent_context, screen_memory_frame_at, screen_memory_contact_sheet) with no local-files or offline mode whatsoever, and connection setup requires the unpinned `npx -y @agent-native/core@latest skills add rewind --client <client> --scope user --yes`. It also directs the agent to open a vendor download URL (https://clips.agent-native.com/download). Recalling what a developer saw on screen serves none of the listed lanes.

excluded_skills.name: stay-within-limits
excluded_skills.reason: Matches no capability lane in the selection rule: it is agent-billing-budget infrastructure (pause work when the 5-hour or weekly usage window hits 95%), not a project capability for Go, Twitch, persistence, testing, security, docs, GitHub, dashboard, QA, or durable knowledge. Its wake-prompt/handoff-packet guidance duplicates ground already held by the installed `handoff` skill and by efficient-frontier's handoff packets. Independently it carries a supply-chain concern: the only concrete usage mechanism it names is `npx -y ccusage@latest blocks --active --json` (skills/stay-within-limits/SKILL.md:30) — an unpinned third-party CLI auto-accepted with `-y`, executed on a recurring loop between every wave of work. The abstract alternative ('the host's usage/budget tool') is not a tool this environment exposes, so in practice the unpinned CLI is the skill. If the owner later wants budget throttling for long orchestrations, this becomes HOLD, unblocked by pinning ccusage to an exact version.

excluded_skills.name: visual-recap
excluded_skills.reason: BLOCKER (mandatory hosted MCP): identical to visual-plan and stated even more absolutely — 'The deliverable is ALWAYS a published Agent-Native Plan, created with `create-visual-recap` on the Plan MCP connector — NEVER inline chat content' and 'an inline summary is not a degraded recap, it is the thing a recap replaces.' Local-files mode again routes through unpinned CLI: `npx @agent-native/core@latest plan blocks --out plan-blocks.md`, `npx @agent-native/core@latest plan local check --dir <plan-dir>`, `npx @agent-native/core@latest plan local serve --dir <plan-dir> --kind recap --open`, `npx @agent-native/core@latest plan local verify --dir <plan-dir> --kind recap`. TO UNBLOCK: same as visual-plan (pin the CLI, accept the hosted connector or run a loopback Plan app). Its methodology is genuinely strong and distinct from the installed `code-review` — mechanically deriving data-model / api-endpoint / file-tree / split-diff blocks from a real diff, under an explicit Grounding Rule ('true by construction only if derived from the actual changed lines... A confidently wrong recap is dangerous in a review context'), plus a Security section forbidding secret transcription that mirrors this
